statement: A model car tests a 600-meter closed circuit of flat, uphill, and downhill stretches (all same slope). The speeds $v_s < v_p < v_d$ (uphill, flat, downhill) are integers and the lap always takes 50 seconds. Find all possible $(v_s, v_p, v_d)$.

In $\triangle ABC$ with $a>b$ ($a=BC$, $b=AC$), $M$ = midpoint of $AB$. $\alpha,\beta$ = incircles of $\triangle ACM$, $\triangle BCM$; $A',B'$ = tangency points on $CM$. Prove $A'B' = \dfrac{a-b}{2}$.

Each integer is colored red or blue: for any finite consecutive set $A$, $|\#\text{red}-\#\text{blue}| \leq 1000$. Prove there exists a set of 2000 consecutive integers with exactly 1000 of each color.
$5654_b$ is a power of a prime. Find $b$ if $b>6$.

Isosceles $\triangle ABC$ ($AB=AC$, $\angle A < 60^\circ$). $D\in AC$ with $\angle DBC=\angle BAC$; $E$ = intersection of perpendicular bisector of $BD$ with line through $A$ parallel to $BC$; $F\in$ line $AC$ with $FA=2AC$ ($A$ between $F$ and $C$). Show $EB\parallel AC$ and that the perpendicular from $F$ to $AB$, perpendicular from $E$ to $AC$, and $BD$ are concurrent.

Two magicians: the first sees an $n\times n$ board colored by a spectator with black/white tokens, and the spectator's chosen square $C$; the first flips one token (possibly on $C$); the second (who saw nothing) must guess $C$. For which $n$ do they have a winning strategy?
